binding_mismatch.description: acmodel bindings check|apply: a literal that bindings.json names (entry, its pointer there: /bindings/<index> or /fixed/<index>) does not agree with its threshold, or is not there. path is the file that holds it (schedule.json or a pack file), rule_id its schedule.json rule, and the error's ref the literal's JSON pointer in the file (/rules/<index>/... in schedule.json; /rules when no rule has rule_id). value: the literal (found) is not the threshold's exported value, or its offset in the fact_offset form (expected); check reports it, apply writes the expected value. fact_key, reference_fact (fact_offset form): the fact key of the fact predicate, or of its fact reference (found), is not the threshold's fact or reference_fact (expected). The comparison is not compared: a rule may test the opposite side of a threshold. form: a fact_offset threshold is bound to something other than the offset of a fact reference {"type": "fact", "fact_key", "offset"} in a fact predicate, or a constant threshold to such an offset. literal_missing: the file has no rule rule_id, or the pointer names nothing or no integer (found is the JSON type there).

binding_unbound_literal.description: acmodel bindings check --strict: an integer literal that a fact predicate of a schedule.json rule (rule_id) compares with, its typed value (value/value) or its fact reference's offset (value/offset), is neither bound to a threshold nor listed under fixed in bindings.json, so it is a number without provenance (#424 design 6.3). pointer is the literal's JSON pointer relative to the rule, as bindings.json writes it; path is schedule.json and the error's ref the literal's pointer in it.

binding_unsupported.description: acmodel bindings check|apply: a bound threshold (output, threshold:<id>) of the fact_offset form whose live offset read the account state (reads: the state nodes it read, reading:<fact> and so on, sorted). Its live part is then not one fact plus a constant, which is all a fact reference holds (#386 CF-4), and the tool never writes an account's value as a constant. The scheduler side chooses: a pack publishes the derived fact, or a selection document computes it. path is exports.json and the error's ref the threshold's entry in it. A constant threshold that read the account state is export_refused (per_account), as export thresholds refuses it.

cache_entry_corrupt.description: An entry of the cache under paths.state_root (contracts/cli.md, Cache) does not hold what its index names: its value blob (path) hashes to found instead of the value hash it is named by (hash_mismatch), is absent (blob_missing) or cannot be read (blob_unreadable, with exception_type and raw_text), or its index row's value hash or reads do not read (index_invalid; path is the index). key is the node key and kind the node kind. A corrupt entry is never served. acmodel run reports it among the warnings, computes the node again and keeps the new value, so the run's outputs and exit status are those of a run without it; acmodel cache verify reports each such entry as an error and repairs nothing. run_outputs_mismatch (acmodel run, a warning): runs/<run id>/outputs.json (path) held other bytes than this run's outputs for the same run id, which is never expected; the file is replaced.

cache_unavailable.description: The cache under paths.state_root cannot be used, so the command stops; it never computes without it. open: the cache folder or its index (path) cannot be created or opened, the index does not take the WAL journal mode, or its schema is not acmodel.cache.v1 (found is the journal mode or the schema found). read and write: reading or writing the index, a blob or a run's outputs failed (found is used when the index's use counter does not read). evict: removing evicted entries or files failed. exception_type and raw_text are the exception's.

command_crashed.description: An exception that no registered failure path covers ended the command; a defect. The traceback goes to stderr.

config_invalid.description: The configuration cannot be used: LOCALAPPDATA is unset or not absolute (location_invalid), or config.json cannot be read, is not UTF-8 JSON, repeats a key, has an unknown or missing member, or a value of the wrong type. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the member.

data_external_hash_mismatch.description: acmodel check: the local copy of a data table's external dataset (dataset, the file named by its sha256 under paths.datasets) does not hash to the declared sha256; found is its sha256. path is the data file; the error's ref is /external/sha256.

data_external_missing.description: acmodel check: a data table declares an external dataset, and its local copy (dataset, the file named by its sha256 under paths.datasets) is absent or cannot be read (exception_type, raw_text). Fetching it is the data side's work; the tool only verifies. path is the data file; the error's ref is /external.

data_reference_missing.description: acmodel check: a data reference (data:<table>[<key>].<column>, a data set, or lookup) names a table no data file of the model holds, a column the table does not declare, or a key that matches no inline row or has the wrong number of parts (row). path is the file of the expression; the error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression and position the character offset of the reference.

deps_invalid.description: The venv or a pinned package is missing, a package is not at its pin, or the interpreter (or the venv's interpreter) is not Python 3.13. setup_command is the command that creates the venv; setup never replaces a venv of another minor version.

engine_failed.description: An engine call failed (#424 design-py 7.1, 7.3). request is the request's index in the call; a failure of a batch is one entry per request of it, and the call goes on. adapter_error: the adapter answered {"error": {code, detail}} for this request; engine_code is its code, passed through, and engine_detail its detail as canonical JSON. exception: the op raised (op reset: the reset after it; op describe: describe at the start); exception_type and raw_text are the exception's, the traceback is in the worker's log, and the worker is not used again. timeout: the batch took longer than engine.request_timeout_ms per request (timeout_ms is the batch's), or the start longer than engine.start_timeout_ms (op start); the worker is stopped. worker_memory_limit: the worker ran out of memory, at the Job's per-process limit (compute.job.worker_memory_mib). worker_exited: the worker exited before it connected (op start, exit_code). start_failed: the scratch directory, the log or the process could not be made, or the channel did not connect (path, exception_type, raw_text). restart_budget_exhausted: a worker ended abnormally (a crash, a timeout, the memory limit) once more after engine.restart_budget restarts of this pool; the call fails and every worker is stopped (restarts, budget, and the exit_code of the last).

engine_guard_violation.description: A guard of the engine worker caught engine code (#424 design-py 7.3) during the import of the entry and make_engine (import), describe, an op (batch) or reset. write_outside_scratch: an open for writing, or a remove, rename, mkdir, rmdir, truncate, link, symlink or rmtree, of path outside the worker's scratch directory; the operation is refused. unlisted_file: a read of path under the engine's home that neither code nor data of engine.json lists; the fingerprint would miss it. unlisted_module: a module under the home that code does not list: the read of its file (path), or the module found loaded after a stage (module, path). global_state_changed: sys.argv, the working directory, sys.path or os.environ (state) differ after the stage. The call fails and every worker is stopped; an engine that catches the refusal is reported all the same.

engine_import_failed.description: The entry point of engine.json (entry, module:callable) did not import in the worker, or calling it (make_engine) raised (#424 design-py 4.9). exception_type and raw_text are the exception's; the traceback is in the worker's log.

engine_nondeterministic.description: The verify run of a sampled request (engine.verify_sample_milli) gave another outcome than the call: the full request, after reset(), in a fresh worker whose PYTHONHASHSEED is verify_hash_seed instead of hash_seed (#424 design-py 7.3). It catches hash or set order, state carried between calls and an untruthful depends_on (a cached result reused for another request). ref is the JSON pointer of the first difference in the result (empty when the verify run failed). The call fails and nothing of it is kept in the cache.

engine_not_configured.description: No engines.roots entry of the local configuration names engine_id, so its home is unknown (#424 design D-4); the tool never guesses one.

engine_protocol_error.description: An engine answered outside acmodel.engine.v2 (#424 design-py 7.1); ref is the JSON pointer in that request's result, or in describe's. not_json: a value that is not a JSON value (found names it: a type such as set or tuple, float_not_finite, string_invalid, <type>_key). result_invalid: a result of the wrong shape (expected): not an object, no depends_on, a depends_on id that the request's entities lack, an evaluate result without numeric metrics or with an unknown member, a malformed error. result_count: evaluate or predict did not return a list of one result per request. These fail the requests concerned and the call goes on. describe_invalid: describe disagrees with engine.json (engine_id, version, ops, max_batch) or is malformed; frame_invalid: the worker sent a frame the host cannot read. These two fail the call.

export_refused.description: acmodel export thresholds, and acmodel bindings check|apply for a bound threshold: an output (threshold:<id>) cannot go into a shared output, so nothing is written (contracts/formats.md, Outputs; bindings take only what the export writes). blocked: it cannot be computed; the errors that block it follow, with needed_by. per_account: it read the account state, and a per-account value never enters a shared output (#424, ruling 66); run and explain show it locally. provisional: it is not confirmed. not_integer, out_of_range: its exact value (value) is not an integer (exports.json can declare a round), or lies beyond +-(2^53-1); a value that continuous unknowns leave open is not_integer, with value <low>..<high>. path is exports.json and the error's ref the threshold's entry in it.

export_write_failed.description: acmodel export thresholds: a file of the export (path) or its folder could not be written. The provenance files are written before thresholds.json, so thresholds.json is left as it was when a provenance file fails; nothing is deleted. acmodel bindings apply: a file whose literals it rewrites (path) could not be written; the files written before it stay written, and apply can run again.

expr_dimension_mismatch.description: An operator or function of an expression gets operands whose types do not fit: an amount of one resource with another, an amount with a time, a bare number with a time, a boolean where a number is needed or the reverse (expr/dimensions.py lists the rules). operands are the operands' types (amount:<resource>, time, count, value, none, number, bool); position is the character offset of the operator. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression. acmodel run (contracts/formats.md, The run) adds path, the file, and also refuses: an expression whose type does not fit what its member expects (operator is the member, e.g. when, value, max, every, consumes, moves, general_logic, offset; operands are the expected and the found type; position is the expression's top operator); a reference whose value has no type in the language (operator reference; operands is a preference's JSON type string, array, object or null, or a column's type enum or id); a fact key declared with two dimensions (operator read); a lookup key that does not fit its key column (operator lookup); the variants of a member or the bounds of a range that do not fit each other (operator variants, interval or distribution); a threshold of a boolean (operator threshold, ref in exports.json).

expr_eval_failed.description: Evaluating an expression failed: a division by zero (acmodel run: or by an enclosure that holds 0), clamp with its low bound above its high bound (acmodel run: or bounds whose enclosures may cross), or a value from the model (a reference, flow, lookup or set) that is not of the type the check gave it (expected is that type, or members for a set; found is the value's Python type). value_invalid (acmodel run) also: a member of a random rule outside its domain (contracts/formats.md, Random rules): operator is the member (rate, hard_pity, p_up, spark), position 0, expected probability (0 to 1), positive_probability (above 0, at most 1) or positive_integer, found the value, and the error's ref the member. evaluation_unsupported (acmodel run): the expression reads what this version does not evaluate yet, and found names it: metric, count or pref (a reference of that kind), interval (a lookup key, a bound of a distribution being sampled, or a member of a pity chain, that continuous unknowns leave open; operator is lookup, sample or the member), random (a random:<id> product), external_dataset (a row of an external table), when (a rule's condition), state (max_single_income, which never reads the account state: an income the cap blocks would need a state value, and no storage cap of a store it moves out of bounds it); operator is reference, the function or the member. range_invalid (acmodel run): the bounds of an interval or distribution unknown, evaluated in one scenario, may be out of order: low above high, or a triangular mode outside them, for some value of the unknowns the bounds read; operator is interval, uniform or triangular, position 0, and the error's ref the unknown's range form (/unknowns/<index>/interval or /distribution). budget_exceeded (acmodel run): a pity chain needs more transitions (pulls x pity counts x guarantee states) than random.max_transitions; operator pity_chain, position 0, expected the limit, found the transitions needed, and the error's ref the rule's /logic/pity_chain. Every output that needs it is blocked. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression; acmodel run adds path, the file. acmodel economy: evaluation_unsupported with operator economy is what the economy does not model yet, at the rule, member or period it names, and found names it: month (a period of unit month), exchange, cooldown or objective (a rule of that kind), gate (a flow behind a gate that is neither open nor of origin person, which is never planned), while (a regen's condition other than its store's stop at its storage cap), every (a regen's interval longer than a day that is not a whole number of days, or in the steady state does not divide its cycle), the kind of a subject that a flow, regen, cap or limit cannot have, an on_reach that its cap_kind does not model, unknown (an amount, cap or limit that reads unknowns: the economy solves single values), state (in the steady state, an amount, cap or limit that needs the account state; a move that needs it and does not leave a store with a storage cap), stock (in a plan, an amount that reads a stock the plan itself changes), unbounded_stock (a read cap on a resource with no hard cap) or income (a read cap that blocks an income other than a collection out of a store); position is 0. value_invalid with operator regen and expected positive: a regen's every is not positive.

expr_overflow.description: A literal, a value read or an intermediate result of an expression has a numerator or denominator of more than max_bits bits (configuration key expr.max_bits; durations count in seconds). Nothing wraps or rounds. operator is the operator or function, literal or reference. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression; acmodel run adds path, the file, and blocks every output that needs it. operator tally (acmodel run with unknowns.samples): a sampled value at export precision, the count or the total of a Monte Carlo tally would leave the int64 range (max_bits 63, bits that of the number, position 0); the output is blocked, and the error's ref is the expression the output comes from.

expr_parse_error.description: An expression does not parse (grammar in expr/syntax.py): a character outside the language, a malformed number, an unexpected token or end, an unknown reference kind, a malformed reference (or a set where a value is needed), the member key $ outside a sum or count over its set, an unknown function, a wrong number of arguments, or an argument of the wrong form. position is the character offset; token is the offending text. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression; acmodel check adds path, the file that holds it.

host_gate_paused.description: The host gate holds compute; a later run or check resumes (contracts/cli.md, Host caps). One entry per reason that holds. memory_below_start: the available host memory (available_mib) is below host.memory.start_min_mib (limit_mib) before a batch, or while the gate is paused. memory_below_pause: inside a batch it fell below host.memory.pause_below_mib (limit_mib). quiet_window: the local time is inside host.quiet_windows[window]. pause_file: the file host.pause_file (path) exists. cpu_load: the host CPU load over the last window (load_milli) is above host.cpu.pause_load_milli (limit_milli). plan_above_report: the planned memory of the run (estimate_mib) is above host.memory.report_plan_above_mib (limit_mib), so the run is reported before it starts.

host_job_not_applied.description: The Job object that caps the tool's processes (CPU rate, memory per process, priority class) could not be created (CreateJobObjectW), configured (SetInformationJobObject: set_limits, set_cpu_rate), joined by the current process (AssignProcessToJobObject) or read back (verify: QueryInformationJobObject, IsProcessInJob). In verify, limit names the limit read back with another value than configured (expected, found), or membership when the current process or a child started afterwards is not in the Job. os_error is GetLastError when a call failed. Nothing computes without the Job.

host_priority_not_applied.description: The priority class of compute.priority (expected is its Windows value) is not in effect. set: SetPriorityClass returned 0 (os_error). verify: GetPriorityClass of the current process, or of a child started after the caps, reads another class (found; 0 with os_error when the call itself failed). platform_unsupported: only Windows has a real host layer, so on this platform the caps cannot be applied. Nothing computes at normal priority.

host_reading_failed.description: A reading of the host layer failed, so the gate or the check cannot decide and does not guess. memory: GlobalMemoryStatusEx. cpu_times: GetSystemTimes, or counters that did not advance consistently over a window. pause_file: checking whether host.pause_file exists failed other than by its absence (path, exception_type, raw_text). process: opening or closing a child process to verify it (OpenProcess, CloseHandle). call is the Win32 function and os_error its GetLastError.

lp_dual_disagrees.description: acmodel economy (a warning): HiGHS's marginal (marginal, as an exact fraction) of a price of the steady state lies outside the interval its re-solves at plus and minus one grain give (low, and high, absent when one grain less is infeasible). target is a resource, with step its step in the cycle, or a cap or limit rule. The price stands as the re-solves give it; the marginal is only a cross-check (#424 design-py 4.3). path is model.json.

lp_infeasible.description: acmodel economy: the program of the steady state or of the plan (solve) has no solution, so the rules contradict each other, or a plan's opening stocks contradict them. rules are the rule ids (and readings the fact keys of opening stocks, plan only) of a minimal set that conflicts: each group is dropped in turn, in id order, and stays dropped while the rest is still infeasible. A group whose check could not be decided (the node limit, or numerical trouble) is kept and listed in unchecked, so the set may then be larger than minimal. The output is blocked, and so is a plan, which needs the steady state. path is model.json.

lp_numeric_check_failed.description: acmodel economy: a solution of HiGHS, converted to exact fractions with lp.max_denominator, breaks a bound, an integrality or a row of its program when checked exactly. stage is the solve: the optimum, the least losses among the optimal solutions (steady state), or a price re-solve. constraint is the row or the variable (kind:id:step), found its exact left side or value, and bound what it must meet (=, <= or >= a value, integer, or finite; a value or marginal that is not finite is found as its float text, with constraint marginal for a marginal). The output is blocked; nothing is rounded into place. path is model.json.

lp_solve_failed.description: acmodel economy: HiGHS gave no usable solution. unbounded: the objective has no maximum, so the rules let the numeraire grow without end (status 3). solver_status: another status (status, scipy's, with HiGHS's message as raw_text) after a second try without presolve; or no solution where one must exist (status 2: a re-solve with one more grain, or the least losses at the optimum). no_solution (plan): the MILP stopped, at its node limit search.milp_node_limit (node_limit; nodes explored) or otherwise, without any feasible plan. stage: the optimum, the least losses, or a price re-solve. The output is blocked. path is model.json.

model_file_invalid.description: An input file of the model (model, rules, data, sources, exports, bindings, state, preference defaults) is refused by its strict reader (contracts/formats.md), or (acmodel run) a state snapshot names another model: value_invalid at /model_id, expected is the model's id. acmodel bindings reads the files that hold bound literals as strict JSON too (format json for a pack file); of schedule.json (format actingcommand.schedule.v1) it also needs its schema_version, and rules that are objects with distinct string ids (value_invalid at the second id). The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the value (the empty pointer for the whole file); path is the file and format the reader. JSON level: unreadable, bom_present, utf8_invalid (offset), syntax_invalid (line, column), key_duplicate (the repeated key), float_literal, constant_invalid (NaN, Infinity), integer_out_of_range (beyond +-(2^53-1)), string_invalid (a lone surrogate). Shape: type_invalid (expected types), member_unknown, member_missing, member_conflict (two of members that exclude each other; expected lists them), value_invalid (expected values), id_invalid (the id grammar). One error per problem; literal is the offending text.

model_id_duplicate.description: acmodel check: an id is declared twice in one namespace. model: entities, periods, rules and unknowns share one; table: data tables; row: the keys of one table's rows (id joins the key parts with commas); source: sources.json; engine: model.json engines; threshold (acmodel run): the thresholds of exports.json; literal (acmodel bindings): the literals that the bindings and the fixed entries of bindings.json name, by file, rule_id and pointer (id joins them with colons). path and the error's ref are the second declaration, first_path and first_ref the first, which references resolve to.

rule_conflict.description: acmodel check: two active rules of the same kind hold the same subject and slot (contracts/formats.md lists the slot of each kind; slot is cap_kind for cap and per for limit), and neither supersedes the other. id is the later rule, conflicts_with the earlier; the error's ref is the later rule.

rule_cycle.description: acmodel check: rules and unknowns that depend on each other in a loop (via reference: through their expressions, flow functions and gate requirements) or that supersede each other in a loop (via supersedes). members are the loop's nodes, sorted (rule:<id>, unknown:<id> or unknown:<id>.<member>); path and the error's ref point at the first member's first link into the loop.

rule_pending_unbounded.description: acmodel check: a pending rule names no unknown (no_unknown; ref is its status), or only unknowns without a range form (unknown_unbounded; ref is its status), or a rule or unknown references an unknown without a range form in an expression (unknown_unbounded; ref is the expression, position the reference). acmodel run: an expression reads a pending data row, which cannot name an unknown (no_unknown; id is <table>[<key parts joined with commas>]; path and ref are the expression's). Without a range, everything that needs it is blocked.

rule_pref_misplaced.description: acmodel check: an expression reads a preference (pref:<key>) outside a gate rule or an objective's terms (#424 design D-2). id and kind are the rule or unknown (kind unknown) that holds it; the error's ref is the JSON pointer of the expression and position the character offset of the reference.

rule_provenance_missing.description: acmodel check: a rule, an unknown, a data row or a data table has an empty provenance list, or a data row has none and its table gives none. id is the entry's id (a row's key parts joined with commas, a table's id); the error's ref is the empty list, or the row.

rule_reference_missing.description: acmodel check: a reference to a declaration of the model does not resolve to one of the expected kinds (an entity kind, entity, rule, rule.<kind>, unknown, unknown_member, metric, engine, source or param): nothing has that id, it is of another kind (found), or it is a superseded rule (superseded_by), which is never read. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the referring member or expression, and position the reference's character offset in an expression. acmodel run (contracts/formats.md, The run) adds: pref, a preference key (pref:<key>, a gate's prefs) that the preference defaults do not hold; rule.derive, rule.cap, rule.limit, a rule: reference to a rule without a value; resource, store, a cap's subject; rule.flow, a cost or yield (target the activity) or max_single_income (target the cap) with no flow amount behind it; rule.derive and rule.derive.live, the from of a threshold in exports.json, which needs live in the fact_offset form. acmodel bindings adds threshold, the threshold of a binding in bindings.json that exports.json does not list (ref is the binding's threshold).

rule_status_invalid.description: acmodel check: a status outside its closed set: confirmed, pending or provisional for rules and data rows; pending or provisional for unknowns. id is the entry's id; the error's ref is the status.

ruling_overrides_general_logic.description: A note of acmodel run (data.notes, never an error): a derive's value differs from its general_logic, the #425 general rule's value. The value stands, by its provenance (a ruling, say); the difference is reported, never hidden. value and general_logic are their distinct exact values, sorted (one each without variants). path and the note's ref are the general_logic expression.

search_budget_exhausted.description: A warning: a budget stopped a solve before it proved its result, which is shown with proven: false: a result, not necessarily the best one. There is no time limit, so the same inputs stop at the same result. plan (acmodel economy): the plan's MILP stopped before it proved its plan optimal, as at its node limit search.milp_node_limit (node_limit; nodes explored, status scipy's), with a feasible plan that passed the exact check; path is model.json. search (the generic search, core/search.py): it reached search.node_limit (node_limit, nodes) while it evaluated team rows (phase evaluate) or while it searched an assignment of two or more disjoint teams (phase assign); its result is the best assignment it found.

search_failed.description: The generic search (core/search.py; contracts/formats.md, The search) has no result. no_legal_assignment: a team has no legal row (team), or the disjoint teams have no assignment that fills them all (no team). op_missing: the engine (engine_id) lacks evaluate (op), or lacks predict (op) while all teams have more legal rows (space) than search.exact_max (exact_max), so there is nothing to screen with. space_too_large: the product of a team's slot combinations has more rows (rows) than search.screen_max_rows (screen_max_rows); nothing is enumerated. screen_overflow: a team's predict terms, rounded at search.screen_scale, could sum beyond the 64-bit integers of the screen (team). budget_exhausted: search.node_limit (node_limit) was reached (phase) before any assignment of all the teams was evaluated.

state_entity_missing.description: acmodel run: an expression reads an entity of the account state that the state snapshot does not hold: its class (entity_class, absent from the state's entities), the entity (entity:<class>[<id>]), or the entity's attribute. Every output that needs it is blocked; the others are computed. path and the error's ref are the expression, position the reference.

state_reading_missing.description: acmodel run: a reading of the account state is needed and the state snapshot does not hold it: the fact key fact (read:<fact>, a cap's reading, or the reading of an entity that amount:<id> or stock:<id> reads), or entity, a resource or store that declares no reading. There is no fallback to a constant. Every output that needs it is blocked; the others are computed. path and the error's ref are the expression (or a cap's reading), position the reference. acmodel economy (plan): the opening stock of a resource or store, fact its reading, or entity when it declares none and something can lower or cap its stock; the error's ref is the entity, or its reading.

state_reference_missing.description: acmodel check: a reference into the account state does not resolve: a fact key (read:<fact>, live.fact, live.reference_fact) that no entity or active cap of the model declares as its reading, an entity class (entity:<class>) that is not an entity_class entity, or an attribute (target) that its class (entity_class) does not declare. The error's ref is the JSON pointer of the referring member or expression, and position the reference's character offset in an expression.

usage_invalid.description: The command line names no command, an unknown command, or an argument the command does not take, or it lacks an argument the command needs (argument is the argument's name). output_unknown (acmodel explain): the output argument is not an output of the model (rule:<id>, general_logic:<id> or threshold:<id>); argument is the id given. The usage text goes to stderr.

venv_failed.description: Work on the venv failed. inspect: the configured path exists but holds no venv (no readable pyvenv.cfg version); it is refused, never replaced. create: python -m venv failed. install: pip failed. dispatch: the venv's Python could not be started, or a re-dispatched child still did not run in the venv (found is its prefix).
